summary: Moved to the untouched client-completion mechanism and submitted a probe for the protection that surrounds the recovery value replacement. A new source range covers handleCommit's re-propose block, a behavior entry records that the owner re-queues its pending client proposals on its own propose channel and clears them when the committed command is a single NOOP, and a new active question asks whether the client request survives that replacement and whether the original instance produces any reply. The submitted experiment keeps the owner alive while replica 3 - which holds no command - recovers its instance, then drains the owner's propose channel and records the owner's instance status, committed command, remaining pending proposals and reply buffer size. Local native feedback shows the predicted protection: the recovery proposed the NOOP although the owner's prepare reply carried its command, the owner's instance ended COMMITTED with the NOOP, and exactly the pending proposal (command id 77) was re-queued on the owner's channel with no reply bytes for the original instance - so the client's request is not silently consumed, at the cost of a fresh decision. The controller's receipt for that comparison remains outstanding, as does its interpretation.
